name: LLM-QAT: Data-Free Quantization Aware Training for Large Language Models
problem: Post-training quantization works down to 8 bits and then breaks down; quantization-aware training needs the original training data, which is unavailable for most released LLMs.
mechanism: Quantization-aware training made data-free by distilling from the model's OWN generations: the pre-trained model generates the calibration sequence, and those sequences are the student-and-teacher data. Straight-through-estimator gradients on quantized weights, activations and the KV cache simultaneously, with the FP16 frozen copy of the same model as teacher. Being data-free, it works on any released generative model.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): LLaMA 7B / 13B / 30B quantized down to 4 bits, with 'large improvements over training-free methods, especially in the low-bit settings'. COMPRESSION RATIO: 4-bit weights + activations + KV cache (16 -> 4 bit on all three). QUALITY COST: not stated as a number in the abstract; the key comparative numbers come from SpinQuant, which reports LLM-QAT trailing by 19.1 points of zero-shot reasoning accuracy at W4A4KV4 on LLaMA-2 7B - i.e. the LLM-QAT 4-bit configuration is roughly 19 points worse than the rotation-based methods, which is a real and often-cited quality gap.
